components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The primary next step; bold, high-contrast, and sized for confident tapping.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 58px; padding: 13px 22px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 10px; border: 1px solid var(--teal); border-radius: 12px; color: var(--white); background: var(--teal); font: 700 1rem/1.45 "Noto Sans", sans-serif; text-align: center; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 180ms ease-out, transform 180ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary svg { width: 20px; height: 20px; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 2; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--teal-dark); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--paper), 0 0 0 6px var(--orange); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(0); }

components.css: .ds-lesson-card { padding: 20px 18px; display: grid; gap: 10px; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 16px; background: var(--white); } .ds-lesson-label { color: var(--teal); font: 800 0.8rem/1.4 "Noto Sans", sans-serif; } .ds-lesson-card h2 { margin: 0; color: var(--teal); font: 700 clamp(1.55rem, 7vw, 1.9rem)/1.2 "Noto Sans", sans-serif; } .ds-lesson-card p { margin: 0; color: var(--muted); font: 400 1rem/1.6 "Noto Sans", sans-serif; } .ds-card-action { width: 100%; min-height: 58px; padding: 13px 22px; border: 1px solid var(--teal); border-radius: 12px; color: var(--white); background: var(--teal); font: 700 1rem/1.45 "Noto Sans", sans-serif; } .ds-card-action:hover { background: var(--teal-dark); } .ds-card-action:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--paper), 0 0 0 6px var(--orange); } .ds-card-progress { margin-top: 5px; padding-top: 15px; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; border-top: 1px solid var(--line); color: var(--teal); font: 700 0.8rem/1.4 "Noto Sans", sans-serif; }

components.name: Six-Step Progress
components.description: Six numbered markers make orientation visible without relying on color alone.
components.css: .ds-progress { margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 6px; list-style: none; } .ds-progress li { width: 31px; height: 31px; display: grid; place-items: center; flex: none; border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 50%; color: var(--muted); background: var(--paper); font: 700 0.78rem/1 "Noto Sans", sans-serif; transition: background-color 250ms ease-out, transform 250ms ease-out; } .ds-progress .ds-complete { border-color: var(--teal); color: var(--white); background: var(--teal); } .ds-progress .ds-current { border: 2px solid var(--teal); color: var(--ink); background: var(--orange); transform: scale(1.08); } .ds-progress li:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--paper), 0 0 0 6px var(--orange); }

narrative.overview:
Saathi makes digital learning feel like a calm, well-spaced workbook: warm paper holds the page, deep teal gives the learner a clear next action, and sage margins give progress room to breathe. The system is friendly and practical rather than technical; large readable type, clear labels, and generous touch-sized controls make every step feel approachable.

On the shipped desktop home screen, a broad two-column lesson introduction balances copy with a drawn practice-phone scene, then resolves into three benefit columns and a quiet safety promise. At 390px, the Urdu experience switches to right-to-left Nastaliq and replaces that desktop hero with a stacked welcome and prominent lesson card; its full-width continue action and six-step path stay together in the first viewport. Across the lesson flow, the current instruction and its labelled fictional-phone action remain distinct but connected, and mistakes receive reassuring, actionable recovery.
keyCharacteristics: Warm ivory reading canvas with restrained, functional teal emphasis.
Visible progress steps, with orange reserved for the current step.
Bilingual Noto Sans / Noto Nastaliq Urdu typography and true RTL flow.
Safe, fictional practice screens with plain-language guidance and recoverable states.

rules.name: The Workbook Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal carries the action and the learning structure; orange marks the current step only. Keep the two roles distinct.

rules.name: The Urdu Line-Breath Rule
rules.body: Urdu content uses the Noto Nastaliq Urdu stack, 2 line-height for general content, and 1.9 for headings, buttons, and selects. Preserve enough vertical space for the script's descending forms.

rules.name: The Quiet Lift Rule
rules.body: Reserve the soft shadow for the hero illustration; use paper, sage, and fine dividers to distinguish routine learning surfaces.

dos: Do use the documented warm-ivory, deep-teal, soft-sage, warm-orange, charcoal, and white palette for their established roles.
Do keep primary learning actions at least 44px high; the canonical primary button is 58px high.
Do show step number or completion mark as well as color, and keep the active step visibly outlined.
Do use Noto Nastaliq Urdu with the documented taller line-height and true RTL direction for Urdu.
Do use plain, reassuring feedback and label simulated phone actions as practice.
donts: Don't compress the interface into dense dashboard rows or small-print instructions.
Don't use orange as a second competing primary-action color.
Don't indicate progress, permission state, or errors by color alone.
Don't present fictional practice as a real call, real contact list, or real camera/microphone permission prompt.
Don't flatten Nastaliq line-height to the Latin rhythm.
